test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Professor Sehgal will organise a webinar on investment tomorrow.

options.text: A webinar on investment is being organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment will have been organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.
A webinar on investment is going to be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow.

solution:
The correct answer is '**A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given above sentence is in an '**active voice form**', hence we need to convert it into a '**passive voice form**'.
 
• In an **active voice**, a **sentence emphasizes the subject**, performing an action.
 
• In a **passive voice**, a **sentence emphasizes the action or the object** of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice** and '**Professor Sehgal**' is the **subject **and '**a webinar**' is the **object**.
 
• When we** convert this sentence into passive voice**, the **subject **'Professor Sehgal' of the active voice **becomes the object**, the object 'a webinar' becomes the **subject**.
 
• Let's have a look at the **structural form** of the given rule:
 
 
• **​Subject + will/shall + V1 + object. (active voice)**
 
• **object + will/shall + be+ V3 + by + subject. (passive voice)**
 
 
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the **future simple tense**.
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *Kriya will sew the bag. (active voice)*
 
• *The bag will be sewed by Kriya. (passive voice)**​​*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that ‘A webinar on investment will be organised by Professor Sehgal tomorrow’ is the correct passive form of the given sentence.
